notes.decision: Translated 'the beam' tentatively. Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲥⲁⲓⲏ/ⲥⲁⲏ 'beam, log, post' (Crum 372a). The image fits the immediately following passage about being 'crucified upon the Enemy' (lines 4-5): the Enemy is figured as the eschatological stake/gallows on which sinners are bound. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the desolation.' Most likely ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲣ̄-ⲭⲁⲣⲉ where ⲭⲁⲣⲉ = Greek χήρα 'widow' (Lyc. orthography), giving the abstract 'state-of-being-widowed' = desolation/destitution. Eschatological term for the condition of sinners bound in the bōlos. Alternative analysis: ⲣ̄ϣⲱⲣⲉ 'plundering' with Lyc. ϣ→ⲭ. Confidence low.

Translated 'sojourn.' Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲣ̄-ϣⲙ̄ⲙⲟ 'be a stranger, sojourn,' with ⲗ for ⲙ. Fits the image of the damned being 'foreigners' confined to the bōlos as their last dwelling-place. Confidence moderate.

notes.coptic_form: ⲛⲍⲩⲡⲟⲗⲓⲟⲛ ⲍⲓ ⲭⲁⲡⲭⲡ ⲍⲓ ⲍⲁⲃⲥ ⲁⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ
notes.decision: Triple identification of the bōlos: 'as ember-pit, as gloom, as shadow without number.' ⲍⲩⲡⲟⲗⲓⲟⲛ tentatively read as Greek ζωπύριον 'live-coal/ember-pit' (other possibilities: σπήλαιον 'cave,' or a κοπρών-type term for filth-pit). ⲭⲁⲡⲭⲡ a reduplicated form, taken as Lyc. ϣⲁⲡϣⲡ̄ 'gloom, dimness.' ⲁⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ tentatively privative ⲁⲧ-ⲏⲡⲉ 'without number/uncountable' (alternative: ⲁⲧ-ⲉⲓⲃⲉ 'without thirst'). All three lexemes uncertain.

Translated 'of boundary.' Likely Lyc. form of ⲧⲱϣ/ⲧⲁϣ 'border, boundary, limit.' The 'stone of boundary' is the boundary-stone marking the irrevocable separation between Light and Darkness — a barrier set with a great guard. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'strike.' Recurring on this page (lines 12, 17, 30) as the verb governing ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ ('plague, blow') and the Enemy. Most likely Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲱϩ/ⲧⲱϩⲥ̄ 'strike, smite, anoint.' Fits both the cosmological barrier-context (12) and the heading-context (17, 30). Translated consistently throughout.

ⲍⲛⲁⲟ̄ⲣⲏⲛ taken as ⲍⲛ̄ + ⲛⲁⲟ̄ + ⲣⲏⲛ ('in great distance/distance-element'); ⲉⲩⲡⲁⲣⲭ as Lyc. ⲡⲱⲣⲭ̄ 'separate' (rather than Greek ὑπάρχω). Translated 'at great distance, separated from one another' to render the spatial-cosmological image of the Light/Enemy enmity preserved by absolute remove.

The chapter heading runs across lines 16-17. ⲉⲧⲁⲩ at end of line 16 best read with ⲧⲉⲍⲟ at beginning of line 17 as a single relative-perfect verb form: ⲉⲧⲁⲩⲧⲉⲍⲟ 'which they have struck' or simply 'which strike' (relative-imperfect). Translated as a continuous heading: 'Concerning the Three Plagues which strike the Enemy on account of the Light.'
Translated 'in the manner in which.' Likely Lyc. ⲛ̄-ϩⲣⲏⲧⲍ or ⲛ̄-ⲧ-ϩⲉ giving 'in the manner.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the carrying-off.' Lexeme uncertain: most likely a verbal noun on ⲱⲗ 'carry, bring, lift' with relational/intensifying prefix ⲣⲁ-, giving 'the (great) carrying-off / final-extraction.' The next line specifies it as the cosmic event 'when they shall separate every thing forth' — fitting an eschatological gathering/extraction. Confidence low.
